rows.evidence: Q1: Section 6.2.4 and Tables 10-12 report the authors' own on-farm data from 71 farmers' fields in western Uttar Pradesh (water productivity, yield, earthwork cost) and Section 3.3 reports their own PRA survey in 10 villages, so the bulletin contains original data alongside synthesised material.
rows.notes: The study is a technical bulletin on laser land leveling under surface (flood/basin) irrigation in rice-wheat systems of the Indo-Gangetic Plains. It contains no data on drip or subsurface drip irrigation, nor on SSDI combined with conservation agriculture. Its own results concern water saving and water productivity from precision land leveling (e.g., Table 10: rice water productivity 0.49 to 0.61 kg/m3 across 71 farms; Fig. 26-28 water use reductions in wheat and rice), which is a different technology from the one in the passage. Q1 is marginal: the document is partly an overview/extension bulletin, but it does report its own survey and on-farm results.

rows.evidence: Q1: Section 6.2.4 and Tables 10-12 report the authors' own on-farm data from 71 farmers' fields in western Uttar Pradesh and Section 3.3 reports their own PRA survey in 10 villages.
rows.notes: The study concerns laser land leveling, not drip/SSDI, and reports nothing on resilience or risk management under drip irrigation. Its own results on risk-related outcomes are limited to laser leveling reducing the coefficient of variation of yield and water productivity among 71 farmers (Tables 10 and 11) and claims about more uniform crop stands under leveled fields. No evidence on the technology in the passage.

notes: Document is Rice-Wheat Consortium Technical Bulletin 7 on laser land leveling; it mixes literature synthesis with original on-farm and PRA data from western Uttar Pradesh. The text appears complete (abstract through annexure and glossary). Figures are not readable, so some results (Figs. 26-35) are known only from captions and text. Neither claim row concerns laser leveling, so both rows are technology mismatches.
